title: The Siege of Concórdia
summary: The southern highlands, 2780. The army's southern column lays siege to the city of gears. Father Ferrer comes with it as Rome's witness.

labels.fresh: FRESH: the city fought first. Its wall is not finished and its army is out on the roads: a true siege.
labels.grown: GROWN: the city waited a year. Its wall is finished, the bolt-throwers stand on it, owls fly over the camp.

sides.name: The Southern Column
sides.about: Father Ferrer, Jakob, General Ruggieri's siege train and the army's southern column on the plateau before Concórdia; the valley's militia.

sides.name: The City
sides.about: Concórdia: its wall, its works, its machines, and the great spring that drives them.

objectives.text: Keep Jakob alive: he hears the city's ticking. Nothing will bring him back if he falls.
Knock down a gate with the guns. The weak ones are marked (their stop-works were taken out).

objectives.phone: Two pioneers to the old mine's mouth (north of the camp).

objectives.phone: Blow the siege park's magazine or bring down Father Ferrer.

k_open1.text: Father Ferrer was old by then. Rome sent him to the highlands anyway, to see the city of gears with his own eyes.

k_open2.text: His report is on my desk still. He wrote it as a priest writes: what he saw, and nothing he did not.

f_open1.text: Concórdia, 2780. The army's southern column came up onto the plateau in the dry winter. General Ruggieri had the guns. I had Rome's letter.

f_open_fresh.text: We had come early. The city had not finished its wall, and its machines were out on the southern roads.

f_open_grown.text: We came a year late. The wall was finished, brass on timber, and the great bolt-throwers stood on it.

f_open_jakob.text: Jakob had come with me from Fürth, an old man now. He said he could hear the city ticking from the road.

f_open_nojakob.text: Jakob was not with me. I had his log of Nuremberg, and I read it every night by the lantern.

f_open_held.text: The jungle front had held. The army came south with the river towns safe behind it.

f_open_thin.text: The jungle front was thin when the army left it. Nobody spoke of it on the road south.

k_open_c.text: Ferrer tells it from the lines. Here it is from inside the wall, where nobody wrote anything down.

cn_open.text: The plateau is full of the Crown's tents. The city's works turn day and night. Nobody in the council says who gives the orders.

r_lines.text: Dig in, Father. Three batteries, one before each gate. Nobody walks up to that wall in daylight.

n_lines.text: THE LINES: your pioneers (the Labourers) dig the marked earthworks before the three gates. Select them and right-click a marked palisade. Then bring the guns up behind the earthworks.

n_dusk.text: The city's machines come out at nightfall. Get the lines dug before then.

j_weak.text: The north gate and the south gate, Father. Their stop-works are gone. I hear them run on, a beat too fast. They will break first.

n_weak.text: Jakob marked the two weak gates (pinged). Your guns knock them down sooner than the others.

f_hollweg.text: On the wall by the great spring stood an old man in a master's coat. He was watching our guns.

j_hollweg.text: It is the Meister. He does not see us, Father. He is listening to the city.

h_prisoner.text: I asked to come, Father. I know the city's ways in. Let me show them, and then do with me what Rome asks.

f_prisoner.text: Stand by me and say what you see. That is all Rome asks of you today.

a_hello.text: The valley is here, Father. We fought that city the day it was founded. We will fight it now.

a_hello_few.text: A few of the valley came, Father. The rest gave their word to the city once, and keep it.

n_probe.text: A few machines come out of the north gate at the diggers.

n_probe2.text: Machines out of the south gate.

n_owls_camp.text: Brass owls over the camp: the city sees everything you do. Muskets at them.

r_charges.text: Father, the Armoury. Prepared charges, the powder bagged ready, and the gunner's quadrant. My guns will fire faster and farther.

n_lines_done.text: The lines are dug. Set the guns behind the earthworks: at nightfall the city comes out.

n_charges_done.text: The guns have their prepared charges.

n_night.text: Night. The city comes out of its gates. THE SORTIES: beat each one back at the batteries.

f_night.text: We heard them before we saw them: the ticking under the wall, then the gates.

n_s1.text: Brass owls out of the dark, and machines with chains at the west gate.

n_s2.text: Dawn. Clock Soldiers out of the north and the south gates.

n_s3.text: The last sortie, the heaviest, out of the west gate: a Pendulum among them.

n_s3_grown.text: Behind them, a bolt-thrower on its cog wheels. Its screw goes through one man into the next.

f_log.text: I read the log again by the lantern. The west gate: its stop-work was taken out, as at Nuremberg. I marked it for the guns.

m_postern.text: The postern by our old quarter is still ours, Father. It opens for you, and not for them.

n_breach.text: A gate is down. The way into the city is open.

j_hurt.text: I'm hit, Father. It is nothing. I'll walk back.

f_jakob_down.text: He had walked from Nuremberg to the end of the world to stand by me. I buried him on the plateau, facing the city.

n_sorties_done.text: The sorties are beaten back. The city shuts its gates.

n_full_day.text: Full day. The city calls its machines back behind the wall.

n_mine.text: THE MINE: bring at least two pioneers to the old mine's mouth in the north of the camp. They go down the old galleries, under the wall, to the great spring's tower.

j_mine.text: The old adits, Father. I hear the spring down there, louder than up here. The galleries go right under its tower.

h_mine.text: I set the spring over the old shaft myself. The galleries run under it. Send your men down.

f_mine.text: Jakob's log had the mine's plan, copied at Fürth from the guild's own papers. The galleries ran under the spring.

n_reserve.text: Your pioneers have all fallen. Three more come up from the baggage at the camp.

n_under.text: The pioneers are under the ground. Hold the mine's mouth until they reach the spring.

r_under.text: The city knows. Here they come. Hold the mouth!

n_spring_down.text: The great spring's tower falls into the old shaft. Every machine in Concórdia runs down where it stands.

f_spring1.text: The ticking stopped. For the first time in seven years the city was quiet.

f_spring2.text: We did not take it. We had not come to take it. We had come to stop it.

n_back.text: The pioneers come back up the gallery.

n_hold.text: THE GREAT SORTIE: the city comes out with everything. Hold the camp and the siege park until dusk.

j_dig.text: Father, under us. Picks, and a spring. They are in the old galleries, coming to the camp.

f_dig.text: In the night the sentries heard digging under the camp. The galleries were the city's now.

n_diggers.text: The city's machines are coming up the old mine's mouth in the north of the camp. Have men there when they come up.

n_up.text: They come up at the old mine's mouth!

n_wave.text: Another wave out of the gates.

n_wave_big.text: Out of every gate at once, with the bolt-throwers.

n_dusk_end.text: Dusk. The city's machines go back behind the wall. The siege holds the road, and nothing more.

f_grown_end.text: We held the road. The wall held the city. Neither of us moved for a year.

n_park_down.text: The siege park's magazine goes up. The column goes back down off the plateau.

f_hurt.text: A scratch. I have been hurt by worse things than a machine.

cn_1.text: You are the city: its works, its gates, its machines on the wall. The Crown digs its lines on the plateau. Break the siege: blow the siege park's magazine in the camp, or bring down the old priest, Father Ferrer.

cn_k7.text: The arsenal's Heavy Works makes Spring Ballistas; its Escapement teaches the Netters the Long Chain. The plates under the streets keep everything wound.

cn_more.text: More machines come out of the works: they are yours.

cn_mine.text: Something moves in the old galleries under the wall, toward the great spring.

cn_won.text: The siege park's magazine goes up. The Crown's column goes back down off the plateau.

cn_ferrer.text: The old priest falls before the wall.

cn_lost_spring.text: The great spring falls into the shaft. The city runs down.

cn_lost_dusk.text: Dusk. The siege still holds the road.

f_end_close.text: I wrote to Rome that the city was crippled, not taken. Its works still turned, slowly, without their great spring.

f_end_held.text: I wrote to Rome that the city stood whole behind its wall, and the Crown held only the road.

f_end_jakob.text: Jakob walked the lines with me every night after. He said the city ticked like a sick man's heart.

f_end_nojakob.text: I have Jakob's log on my desk. I have written his name at the end of it.

f_end_walls.text: Hollweg stood on his wall to the end. He never looked away from his city.

f_end_prisoner.text: Hollweg asked to see the lines at the end. He stood there a long time, and then asked me to hear his confession.

k_end1.text: Ferrer's report came to Rome in the spring. I read it twice.

k_end_close.text: The city of gears was crippled that year. Not dead. Crippled things do not stop; they limp.

k_end_held.text: The city of gears stood whole behind its wall. It had been given a year, and it had used every hour of it.

k_end_fresh.text: And all that year the swarm came down the rivers, while the army was in the south.

k_end_grown.text: Two fires, and the army had gone to both. Neither was out.

k_end_c.text: That is not how it went. The siege held. Hear it again from Ferrer.

new_charges.text: NEW: PREPARED CHARGES. Research it at the camp's Armoury (it needs the Foundry): the powder comes in ready-made bags, and every Field Cannon and Mortar reloads a fifth faster. Against plates that must be hit again and again, it is the guns' science.

new_quadrant.text: NEW: THE GUNNER'S QUADRANT. Research it at the Armoury after Prepared Charges: the guns are laid by the quadrant, and every Field Cannon and Mortar reaches a tile farther, from behind the earthworks to the gates.

new_ballista.text: NEW: THE SPRING BALLISTA. Made at the arsenal's Heavy Works: a bolt thrower on cog wheels whose screw goes through its target into the men behind. Hard on guns and earthworks; it cannot shoot what is close or in the air.

new_long_chain.text: NEW: LONG CHAIN. Research it at the arsenal's Escapement: every Netter throws its net much farther, from behind the Clock Soldiers onto the gunners.

rome.caption: Rome, the present. The King tells it.

text_if.text: The great spring's tower was blown from the old mine: the city is crippled and besieged.
The army holds the road, but the city stands whole behind its wall.
Jakob is not with Father Ferrer.

city.title: The City
city.text: The siege of Concórdia was broken.

text: The southern highlands, 2780. You are the army's southern column before Concórdia: Father Ferrer, Jakob, General Ruggieri's siege train, Musketeers and Guardsmen, Cuirassiers and the pioneers who dig.
Dig the siege lines before the three gates, beat back the city's sorties, and keep the siege park's magazine standing.
If the city was fought first, its wall is unfinished: the old mine runs under it. If it waited a year, hold the road against everything it has.
The southern highlands, 2780. You are Concórdia: its wall, its arsenal in the old Nuremberg quarter, its machines and the great spring on the mine hill.
Break the siege: blow the siege park's magazine in the Crown's camp, or bring down Father Ferrer, before the Crown's work is done.
